description: Bipolar (BJT) Transistor NPN 160V 600mA 100MHz 300mW Surface Mount SOT-23

provenance.pins: datasheet p.1 Function Diagram, SOT-23: 1 B, 2 E, 3 C
provenance.vbe: inferred - silicon junction at 800 uA over temperature; not in the datasheet

designVerdict: SELECTED as Q3, the emitter follower feeding the HUSB238A VBUS pin. MMBT5551, SOT-23, 160 V VCEO.
notes: Replaces the BSS138 (C7420339) in the follower role only - Q1/Q2, the FAULT interlocks, are still BSS138s. The reason is the offset, not the voltage rating. The HUSB238A's undervoltage detector compares its VBUS PIN against a PERCENTAGE of the requested voltage (86% in the 10-26 V band, 80% in 5-10 V), while a follower subtracts a FIXED drop. A fixed offset is a bigger fraction of a smaller contract, so the lower the PDO the worse it gets: the pass condition in the 86% band is V_offset <= 0.09*V, which the BSS138's 1.6 V worst-case V_GS meets only above 17.8 V. The 9 V, 12 V and 15 V contracts all false-disconnected.

A silicon V_BE is 0.6-0.8 V where that gate is 0.8-1.6 V, which moves the floor below 9 V. Worked at V_BE 0.80 V, hFE 60 and R44 = 3.24 kOhm: margins are +0.51 V at 9 V, +0.24 V at 12 V, +0.51 V at 15 V, +0.96 V at 20 V and +2.45 V at 28/36 V. 12 V is the pinch point because it sits just inside the 86% band.

V_BE IS NOT IN THIS DATASHEET. It specifies VCEO 160 V, VEBO 6.0 V, hFE in three rows - 80 min at 1.0 mA, 100-300 at 10 mA, 30 min at 50 mA; the 1.0 mA row brackets this design's 800 uA operating point and VCE(sat), and gives no V_BE(on) at any current. The 0.6-0.8 V used above is a silicon junction at 800 uA over -20 to +85 C - physics, not a published figure - and the 12 V margin rests on it directly. Measure before trusting.

VEBO 6.0 V covers the power-down case: D14 holds the pin at 4.19 V from the 5 V rail while the bus collapses, so the junction sees up to 4.19 V reversed. The datasheet characterises I_EBO at exactly 4.0 V, so that is a region the part is specified in.

VCE at the binding corner - a +5% bus against the lowest emitter the spread allows (Zener low bin 25.65 V less V_BE max 0.80 V = 24.85 V) - is 12.95 V in normal operation and 39.65 V during a 64.5 V TVS clamp, against 160 V. The BSS138's 50 V would have been 1.3x that event.

Base current is the cost: 13 uA at hFE 60, which R44 must supply. R44 is 3.24 kOhm, which puts that IR drop at 43 mV. It is sized small on purpose: the 800 uA it scales with is specified ONLY at VBUS = 5 V (p.6), so the 12 V margin would otherwise hang on an unpublished number. At 3.24 kOhm it stays positive from 800 uA to the 4 mA the datasheet's other VBUS row gives at 29.4 V.
THE ONLY V_BE FIGURE IN THE DATASHEET IS V_BE(sat) <= 1.0 V at I_C = 10 mA with a forced beta of 10. That is deep saturation and does NOT bound the active-region value at 800 uA. Do not reach for it.

The transistor never saturates here: R44 is the only path into the base, so on any contract the Zener does not clamp the base sits below the collector by exactly I_B x R44 ~ 43 mV (at hFE 60; 32 mV at the datasheet's 80 min). At 28 V and 36 V the clamp holds the base 7-10 V below the collector instead - the same conclusion with more room. V_BC is never positive, so the part is always inside the active region, which is what makes the V_BE assumption applicable.
